definition: Improve a bad or unsatisfactory situation.
example: Extra support helped ameliorate the effects of isolation.
nuance: Ameliorate is formal and commonly concerns conditions or harmful effects.
prompt: A policy addresses poor living conditions.
options: The reforms can ameliorate conditions by improving access to clean water.
The reforms ameliorated conditions by making them worse.
Ameliorate meant to preserve every existing problem unchanged.
The policy ameliorated conditions simply by describing them.
reasons: Better access improves the unsatisfactory situation.
Worsening is the opposite of improvement.
Preserving problems does not improve them.
Description alone does not improve conditions.

practice.prompt: During exam week, the school library is so crowded that students cannot find seats.
options: Opening two empty classrooms as overflow study space helped ameliorate the crowding.
Squeezing three extra classes into the library ameliorated the crowding until students sat on the floor.
The librarian ameliorated the history and science shelves into a single jumbled section.
The new annex ameliorated the old library by copying its cramped layout exactly.
reasons: Adding seats elsewhere eases a bad situation and makes it more bearable.
Bringing in more people made the crowding worse, the reverse of easing it.
This confuses the word with amalgamate; merging shelves into a jumble fixes nothing.
Copying a model is emulating, and repeating a cramped design does not ease crowding.
